authority.documentTitle: Procedural Dungeon Generator: Governed Webpage Projection
futureStatePreview: One admitted contract projects the playable dungeon page, its three closed decision ontologies, their adapter modules, and the architecture review document used to inspect all of it.

Movement legality, per-cell render role, and keyboard-to-command translation are governed ontology data, not authored branching in the page; only procedural generation and the visibility sweep remain authored algorithms, and that boundary is recorded as an explicit contract deviation rather than left implicit.
reviewChecklist: Movement legality is decided by the dungeon-movement ontology, not by an authored if/else in the page.
Every cell's render role (hidden / visible-floor / visible-wall) is decided by the dungeon-render-role ontology, including the God Mode override.
Every admitted keyboard key is translated by the dungeon-keyboard-command ontology; unmapped keys are rejected, not silently ignored by authored logic.
The three adapter modules are each exactly one import, one function, one semantic invocation, one direct return -- verified structurally, not by inspection.
The browser page's vendored execution logic is proven equivalent to direct semantic execution for every canonical fixture, not merely asserted.
Procedural generation and the multi-ray visibility sweep are explicitly declared as authored-algorithm deviations, not silently unproven ontology claims.
The rendering frame is data (an operations list) computed before any canvas call; the canvas adapter applies it without making rendering decisions.

reviewerPerspective.objective: to confirm which parts of the dungeon page are governed ontology decisions and which parts remain authored algorithms, and to verify both classes independently
reviewerPerspective.outcome: the team can sign off on the page knowing exactly which behaviors are provably closed and which are explicitly, not silently, out of that closure

decisions.statement: Model every player action as one pure oldState -> newState call through the ontology runtime rather than adding a session/turn primitive.
Extend the runtime with closure-provable bounded arithmetic (exhaustive range proof over small declared domains) rather than a general expression primitive.
Movement legality, per-cell render role (including God Mode), and keyboard-to-command translation become real, closed, tested ontologies.

Implement the four new verification concerns (DOM structure, collapsed bootstrap shape, semantic execution equivalence, render command frame) as real, working Node verification scripts wired through the existing command-exit-verifier.v1 mechanism, rather than as new closed-world engine-builtin verifier types with their own registry/digest chain.

The four verification scripts are declared-artifact-scope exempt tooling (not declared artifacts), avoiding the .mjs-extension canonical-lineage responsibility requirement that would otherwise apply to them.

The page's vendored DAG-walk executor omits AJV type re-validation at each primitive step, since type-closure is a governance-time guarantee already proven by the contract's gate, not a per-call runtime necessity.
buildRenderingFrame() emits a declarative pixel-grid-rendering-frame.v1 value before any canvas call; applyRenderingFrame() is a dumb executor with no rendering decisions.

Building a fully generic, registry-integrated single-file-semantic-webpage-projector and four brand-new closed-world engine verifier primitives (reusable across any future web capability, not just this one) is deferred; this contract delivers the concrete, working capability for procedural-dungeon-webpage specifically.

decisions.source: User: rejected relocating BSP/Bresenham into a governed module that still branches; 'purely data-driven', 'pure ontology'
decisions.statement: Extend the runtime a third time: iterate-bounded-worklist.v1 gains guarded (per-step conditional) advance steps, item-field/fact-indexed reads, a seeded-draw operand, and an item-field-length operand; a new resolve-branching-worklist.v1 primitive adds a genuine queue-processing primitive (not flattened recursion) for two-way region splitting.

BSP region-splitting (dungeon-topology), room/corridor rasterization (dungeon-rasterize), and the 76-ray Bresenham visibility sweep (dungeon-visibility) become real, closed, tested ontologies executed by the generic runtime -- no authored branching or iteration remains for these decisions anywhere in the page or its adapters.

decisions.source: Doc section 4 (browser ports vs domain operations)
decisions.statement: buildRenderingFrame()'s single for-loop over the 60x60 display grid contains zero decisions of its own: every per-cell classification is delegated to the dungeon-render-role ontology. This is mechanical repetition of an already-fully-decided call, the same category the doc admits for browser mechanics, not a domain-semantics escape hatch.

deviations.impact: The four checks are real and run at gate time with the same fail-closed semantics, but are contract-declared tooling rather than reusable, generically-typed engine primitives available to other future artifact families without re-authoring the scripts.
deviations.implemented: Four real, working Node scripts perform the same checks and are wired in via the existing command-exit-verifier.v1 mechanism (conformance.artifactEvaluations).
deviations.proposed: Register dom-structure-verifier.v1, collapsed-web-bootstrap-verifier.v1, semantic-execution-equivalence-verifier.v1, and browser-render-command-verifier.v1 as new closed-world engine verifier types in registries/verifier-registry.json.
deviations.reason: Registering genuinely new, generic, registry-integrated verifier types is itself Stage-1-scale engineering (new closed-world proof obligations, digest re-pinning cascading to every existing contract). The command-exit-verifier.v1 extension point already exists precisely for declaring arbitrary verification logic without engine changes.

features.purpose: Generate a dungeon whose floor regions are fully connected.
Resolve whether a movement request lands on floor or is blocked by a wall.
Reveal only the tiles an unobstructed sightline reaches.
Render exactly the authorized dungeon frame.

obligations.statement: Every carved floor region must be reachable from every other floor region through corridors.
A movement request onto a floor tile must authorize the move and advance the position by exactly one tile.
A movement request onto a wall tile must block the move and leave the position unchanged.
Each cell's render role (hidden, visible-floor, visible-wall) must be resolved from exactly its cell value, God Mode state, and revealed state.
The canvas adapter must apply exactly the operations present in the authorized rendering frame and no others.
Every observed keyboard key must translate to exactly one admitted movement command or be rejected as not admitted.
Every cell of the padded grid must resolve to exactly floor or wall from the decided room and corridor rectangles, with no cell left unresolved.
A visibility sweep must reveal a wall tile it reaches and must not reveal any cell beyond that wall along the same ray.

scenarios.purpose: Given an admitted BSP generation authority, every floor region is connected.
One movement command targeting an adjacent floor tile advances the player position by one tile.
One movement command targeting an adjacent wall tile leaves the player position unchanged.
A ray crossing a wall tile reveals the wall tile and no cell beyond it.
Given a canonical dungeon rendering frame, the browser projection applies exactly the declared canvas operations.
The decided BSP topology is rasterized into a dense wall/floor grid with no cell left undecided.
